restoration_note: Teaching describes the descent of the First Man clothed in five garments (the Five Sons / elements as Living Soul) each holding five inner faculties, the joining of Call and Answer that effects ascent, and the liturgical Pentecost as the soul's eating of the Call-Answer as 'living food.' Restorations are constrained mostly by Coptic grammar (article completions, relative converters, perfect prefixes, genitive linkers across line breaks), formulaic doublets (ⲡⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ ⲙⲛ ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ), and Lycopolitan ordinal/numeral conventions (ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲛⲍ̄, ⲛⲓⲁ̄ⲉⲩⲧⲉⲣⲁ). One editor fill at {12} was corrected: 'works of darkness' (ⲕⲉⲕ) fits the spiritual arc of being raised away from darkness-and-below far better than the editor's ⲁⲧⲡ 'those above.' Many fragmentary closing lines (sections 5157, 5161-5163, 5164-5166) were left unrestorable because the surviving traces are too sparse to constrain content beyond syntactic guesswork.
